messages.subject_clean: Latent variable index and dimensions error
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

I'm just starting to use nimble so please bear with me if this is a ridiculously simple question. I've made a function to determine the nearest grid cell to the latent variable location. It runs and compiles just fine but when I use it in the model I get an error.

Function:
nearest <- nimbleFunction(
run = function(x1 = double(1),
x2 = double(1),
y1 = double(1),
y2 = double(1)) {
dist <- numeric(length(y2))
for(i in 1:length(y2)) {
dist[i] <- sqrt(((x1 - y1[i]) ^2) + ((x2 - y2[i]) ^2))[1] }
id <- which(dist == min(dist))
return(id)
returnType(integer(1))
}
)

Model:
for (t in 2:TT){
cell[t] <- nearest(mu[t,1], mu[t,2], S_x, S_y) #nearest neighbour in S to mu[t]
cell.p[t] <- nearest(mu[t-1,1], mu[t-1,2], S_x, S_y) #nearest neighbour in S to mu[t-1]
delta.d[t] <- (dist[cell[t], cell.p[t]]) #distance between 2 locations - dist is standardized so I don't think I need to standardize delta.d
X.match[t] <- cell[t] #I likely don't need this
mu[t,1] <- expit((beta1*x1[X.match[t]] + beta2*x2[X.match[t]] + beta3*x3[X.match[t]]) - (delta.d[t]/(delta.t[t]*phi)))
mu[t,2] <- expit((beta1*x1[X.match[t]] + beta2*x2[X.match[t]] + beta3*x3[X.match[t]]) - (delta.d[t]/(delta.t[t]*phi)))
#observation model
s_lon[t] ~ dt(mu = mu[t, 1], sigma = sigma_lon, df = nu_lon)
s_lat[t] ~ dt(mu = mu[t, 2], sigma = sigma_lat, df = nu_lat)

Error is:
Error in genVarInfo3() :
  Dimension of cell is 0, which does not match its usage in 'delta.d[t] <- (dist[cell[t], cell.p[t]])'.

Any help is much appreciated!

Cheers

messages.subject: Creating a matrix
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm using nimble for a population dynamics model that uses a lot of matrices with stochastic entries. I tried to define the matrices but keep running into errors. Here's a reproducible example of the problem. Is there a way to get the first version to work, or do I have to define matrices one column at a time?
Thank you!

code1 <- nimbleCode({
  p1 ~ dunif(0,1)
  p2 ~ dunif(0,1)
  # Version 1, this produces an error:
  P[1:2,1:2] <- matrix(c(p1*p2,p2, p1,p1), nrow = 2, ncol = 2)
  # Version 2, this works:
  # P[1:2,1] <- c(p1*p2,p1)
  # P[1:2,2] <- c(p2,p1)
  x[1,1:2] <- x0[]
  for(t in 1:4){
    x[t+1,1:2] <- P[1:2,1:2]%*%x[t,1:2]
    y[t] ~ dnorm(x[t+1,1], var = p1*p2)
  }
})
Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code1,
                      dimensions = list(x = c(5,2)),
                      data = list(y=c(6,8,11,12), x0 = c(3,5)),
                      inits = list(p1 = 0.5, p2 = 0.5))
mcmc.out <- nimbleMCMC(Rmodel, niter = 100, nchains = 2, monitors = c("p1", "p2"))

Thanks for catching and reporting the issue.

My supervisor and I just submitted a paper for my thesis to the arxiv. The paper is about modeling zero-inflated spatio-temporal infectious disease counts..

I thought I would share the paper and code as it makes extensive use of Nimble's custom sampler feature, and so it might be useful as a illustration for how custom samplers work. Specifically, the custom samplers are blocked forward filtering backward sampling samplers for coupled Markov switching (hidden Markov) models (see paper for more details). They are similar to the standard FFBS samplers which are quite popular for hidden Markov models.

Thanks to everyone in the community who helped in both writing the samplers and figuring out how to do efficient model calculations.

paper - https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.02334

code -  https://github.com/Dirk-Douwes-Schultz/ZS_CMSP_code

messages.body_plain:
Hi!

I've been having issues recovering my "true" values with the distribution I created below. I've been able to recover the true values using nimble's distribution, but not with my own.

Distribution functions
rMVNkron <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(n = integer(), mu_vec = double(1), cov_mat = double(2), corr_mat = double(2)) {
    returnType(double(1))
    kron_mat <- nim_kron(cov_mat, corr_mat)
    ch <- chol(kron_mat)
    return(rmnorm_chol(1, mu_vec, ch, prec_param = FALSE))
  }
)

dMVNkron <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(1), mu_vec = double(1), cov_mat = double(2), corr_mat = double(2),
                 log = logical(0, default = 1)) {
    returnType(double())
    r <- dim(cov_mat)[1]
    q <- dim(corr_mat)[2]
    xm_mat <- matrix((x-mu_vec), q, r)

    logProb <- (-1/2) * (r*q*log(2*pi) + q*logdet(cov_mat) + r*logdet(corr_mat) +
                           sum(diag(inverse(corr_mat) %*% t(xm_mat) %*% inverse(cov_mat) %*% xm_mat)))
    return(logProb)
  }
)

I will eventually be running my simulation on a large amount of data, with the Kronecker product of an 81x81 covariance matrix and 31x31 correlation matrix. So I created this new distribution to handle the Kronecker product more efficiently.

I've tested that my density and random generator work as expected in base R. However, every time I run a simulation with my distribution, I get very small values for `rho1` and `rho2`.

I've attached an R script that fully replicates the issue I'm having (includes two models - one with nimble's distribution and one with my own), including the fake data I've been using.

I'd really appreciate any thoughts you may have on why this is happening and/or if you notice problems with my density or simulation functions.

Thank you so much for your help!

Best,
Liz

library(LearnBayes)

n <- 100

mu <- rep(0,9)
y <- rmnorm(n, mean = mu, varcov = kron_matrix) # using rmnorm from LearnBayes package

nim_mat <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(vector = double(1)) {
    returnType(double(2))
    dims_mat <- sqrt(length(vector))
    return(matrix(vector, nrow = dims_mat, ncol = dims_mat))
  })

kronecker <- function(mat_A, mat_B) {return(mat_A %x% mat_B)}
nim_kron <- nimbleRcall(function(mat_A = double(2), mat_B = double(2)) {},
                        returnType = double(2), Rfun = "kronecker")

## model, with nimble's distribution --------
rho_codev1 <- nimbleCode({
  # priors on rho1 and rho2
  rho1 ~ dbeta(4,6); rho2 ~ dbeta(4,9)
  constraint_rho ~ dconstraint(rho1 + rho2 < 1)

  og_mat[1:3,1:3] <- nim_mat(c(1, (rho1 + rho2), rho2, (rho1+rho2), 1, 0, rho2, 0, 1))
  full_mat[1:9, 1:9] <- nim_kron(og_mat[1:3, 1:3], diag(3))

  # likelihood

  }
})

data <- list(y = y, constraint_rho = 1)
inits <- list(rho1 = runif(1), rho2 = runif(1))

conf_rho <- configureMCMC(rho_v1, useConjugacy = FALSE)
mcmc_rho <- buildMCMC(conf_rho)

comp_rho <- compileNimble(rho_v1, mcmc_rho, resetFunctions = TRUE)
samples_v1 <- runMCMC(mcmc = comp_rho$mcmc_rho, niter=5000, nburnin = 1000) %>% as.matrix() %>% mcmc()

plot(samples_v1)

## new distribution to incorporate covariance and correlation matrices as a kronecker product ------

rMVNkron <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(n = integer(), mu_vec = double(1), cov_mat = double(2), corr_mat = double(2)) {
    returnType(double(1))
    kron_mat <- nim_kron(cov_mat, corr_mat)
    ch <- chol(kron_mat)
    return(rmnorm_chol(1, mu_vec, ch, prec_param = FALSE))
  }
)

dMVNkron <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(1), mu_vec = double(1), cov_mat = double(2), corr_mat = double(2),
                 log = logical(0, default = 1)) {
    returnType(double())
    r <- dim(cov_mat)[1]
    q <- dim(corr_mat)[2]
    xm_mat <- matrix((x-mu_vec), q, r)

    logProb <- (-1/2) * (r*q*log(2*pi) + q*logdet(cov_mat) + r*logdet(corr_mat) +
                           sum(diag(inverse(corr_mat) %*% t(xm_mat) %*% inverse(cov_mat) %*% xm_mat)))
    return(logProb)
  }
)

## model with my distribution ---------
rho_codev2 <- nimbleCode({
  # priors on rho1 and rho2
  rho1 ~ dbeta(4,6); rho2 ~ dbeta(4,9)
  constraint_rho ~ dconstraint(rho1 + rho2 < 1)

  og_mat[1:3,1:3] <- nim_mat(c(1, (rho1 + rho2), rho2, (rho1+rho2), 1, 0, rho2, 0, 1))
  iden[1:3, 1:3] <- diag(3)

  # likelihood
  for(j in 1:n) {
    y[j,1:9] ~ dMVNkron(mu[1:9], og_mat[1:3,1:3], iden[1:3, 1:3])
  }
})

mcmc_rho <- buildMCMC(conf_rho)

comp_rho <- compileNimble(rho_v2, mcmc_rho, resetFunctions = TRUE)

plot(samples_v2)

messages.subject: Re: issue with user-defined distribution
messages.body_plain:
Hi Liz,

Looks like there is a math error in your dMVNkron.  Note that in

inverse(corr_mat) %*% t(xm_mat) %*% inverse(cov_mat) %*% xm_mat

the dimensions don't align - corr_mat is q x q while t(xm_mat) is r x q.
The reason you didn't get an error that would have clued you in is that in your test case r=q=3.

I think you need to put the transpose on the second xm_mat rather than the first, but I haven't gone back and worked through the details of Kronecker product covariance matrices in a multivariate normal to verify this.

Also a side note on computational efficiency. Your dMVNkron uses logdet() and inverse().  These will generally be rather less efficient than taking the Cholesky and making use of that:

 - The log-determinant of a matrix is two times the sum of the log of the diagonal elements of the Cholesky of that matrix
 - And inverse of a matrix times a vector or matrix, X, can be written as:
     ch <- chol(matrix)
     backsolve(ch, forwardsolve(t(ch), X))
  That would remove two of the matrix multiplications in the formula for the logProb.
Finally if you just need the diag of a product of matrices, that is equal to the sum of the direct product of one of the matrices times the transpose of the other, so the final matrix multiplication would not be needed:
   diag(A%*%B) is equal to sum(t(A) * B)

Depending on the size of your matrices, these efficiency issues might not make a big difference or could make a important difference in the speed of your MCMC, in part depending on whether the repeated dMVNkron calculations are the computational bottleneck.

-chris

      +

        (1 - nimStep(N[i,t-1]-0.01)) * exp(rho + S[i] + T[t])

messages.subject: Re: issue with user-defined distribution
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

Apologies for the delay in replying. Thank you so much for catching that error with my dimensions! I went back through my math and realized that cov_mat needed to switch with corr_mat in my logProb formula. After making that change, the distribution worked perfectly and recovered my rho values. And thank you for your recommendations on improving the efficiency. I've included your changes in my distribution and am hoping it speeds things up a bit!

I really appreciate your help!

Best,
Liz

On Thu, Feb 11, 2021 at 10:03 AM Chris Paciorek <christophe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Liz,
>
> Looks like there is a math error in your dMVNkron.  Note that in
> inverse(corr_mat) %*% t(xm_mat) %*% inverse(cov_mat) %*% xm_mat
> the dimensions don't align - corr_mat is q x q while t(xm_mat) is r x q.
> The reason you didn't get an error that would have clued you in is that in your test case r=q=3.
>
> I think you need to put the transpose on the second xm_mat rather than the first, but I haven't gone back and worked through the details of Kronecker product covariance matrices in a multivariate normal to verify this.
>
> Also a side note on computational efficiency. Your dMVNkron uses logdet() and inverse().  These will generally be rather less efficient than taking the Cholesky and making use of that:
>
>  - The log-determinant of a matrix is two times the sum of the log of the diagonal elements of the Cholesky of that matrix
>  - And inverse of a matrix times a vector or matrix, X, can be written as:
>      ch <- chol(matrix)
>      backsolve(ch, forwardsolve(t(ch), X))
>   That would remove two of the matrix multiplications in the formula for the logProb.
> Finally if you just need the diag of a product of matrices, that is equal to the sum of the direct product of one of the matrices times the transpose of the other, so the final matrix multiplication would not be needed:
>    diag(A%*%B) is equal to sum(t(A) * B)
>
> Depending on the size of your matrices, these efficiency issues might not make a big difference or could make a important difference in the speed of your MCMC, in part depending on whether the repeated dMVNkron calculations are the computational bottleneck.
>
> -chris
>
> On Tue, Feb 9, 2021 at 8:54 AM Liz Lawler <esla...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > One quick note: every several times this model runs with the fake data, the initialized covariance matrix in the `rho_v2` model turns out to be singular, so the model doesn't work (as I would expect). When the covariance matrix is nonsingular, the simulation runs appropriately but the densities of `rho1` and `rho2` peak much lower than expected. So if you run the code and it happens to initialize with a singular matrix, that's not the issue I'm referring to!
> >
> > On Monday, February 8, 2021 at 6:53:44 PM UTC-7 Liz Lawler wrote:
> > > I can't seem to attach anything to this post (kept getting an error with the original message)! So I've included the contents of the R script below. Thank you again!
> > >
> > > library(nimble)
> > > library(coda)
> > > library(LearnBayes)
> > > library(tidyverse)
> > >
> > >
> > > ## simulate data --------
> > > rho1 <- 0.3; rho2 <- 0.5 # "true" parameters
> > > varcov <- matrix(c(1, rho1 + rho2, rho2, rho1+rho2, 1, 0, rho2, 0 ,1), 3, 3)
> > > n <- 100
> > > kron_matrix <- varcov %x% diag(3)
> > > mu <- rep(0,9)
> > > y <- rmnorm(n, mean = mu, varcov = kron_matrix) # using rmnorm from LearnBayes package
> > >
> > > nim_mat <- nimbleFunction(
> > >   run = function(vector = double(1)) {
> > >     returnType(double(2))
> > >     dims_mat <- sqrt(length(vector))
> > >     return(matrix(vector, nrow = dims_mat, ncol = dims_mat))
> > >   })
> > >
> > > kronecker <- function(mat_A, mat_B) {return(mat_A %x% mat_B)}
> > > nim_kron <- nimbleRcall(function(mat_A = double(2), mat_B = double(2)) {},
> > >                         returnType = double(2), Rfun = "kronecker")
> > >
> > > ## model, with nimble's distribution --------
> > > rho_codev1 <- nimbleCode({
> > >   # priors on rho1 and rho2
> > >   rho1 ~ dbeta(4,6); rho2 ~ dbeta(4,9)
> > >   constraint_rho ~ dconstraint(rho1 + rho2 < 1)
> > >
> > >   og_mat[1:3,1:3] <- nim_mat(c(1, (rho1 + rho2), rho2, (rho1+rho2), 1, 0, rho2, 0, 1))
> > >   full_mat[1:9, 1:9] <- nim_kron(og_mat[1:3, 1:3], diag(3))
> > >
> > >   # likelihood
> > >   for(j in 1:n) {
> > >     y[j,1:9] ~ dmnorm(mu[1:9], cov = full_mat[1:9, 1:9])
> > >   }
> > > })
> > >
> > > constants <- list(n = n, mu = mu)
> > > data <- list(y = y, constraint_rho = 1)
> > > inits <- list(rho1 = runif(1), rho2 = runif(1))
> > > rho_v1 <- nimbleModel(rho_codev1, constants = constants, data = data, inits = inits)
> > >
> > > conf_rho <- configureMCMC(rho_v1, useConjugacy = FALSE)
> > > mcmc_rho <- buildMCMC(conf_rho)
> > >
> > > comp_rho <- compileNimble(rho_v1, mcmc_rho, resetFunctions = TRUE)
> > > samples_v1 <- runMCMC(mcmc = comp_rho$mcmc_rho, niter=5000, nburnin = 1000) %>% as.matrix() %>% mcmc()
> > >
> > > plot(samples_v1)
> > >
> > > ## new distribution to incorporate covariance and correlation matrices as a kronecker product ------
> > > rMVNkron <- nimbleFunction(
> > >   run = function(n = integer(), mu_vec = double(1), cov_mat = double(2), corr_mat = double(2)) {
> > >     returnType(double(1))
> > >     kron_mat <- nim_kron(cov_mat, corr_mat)
> > >     ch <- chol(kron_mat)
> > >     return(rmnorm_chol(1, mu_vec, ch, prec_param = FALSE))
> > >   }
> > > )
> > >
> > > dMVNkron <- nimbleFunction(
> > >   run = function(x = double(1), mu_vec = double(1), cov_mat = double(2), corr_mat = double(2),
> > >                  log = logical(0, default = 1)) {
> > >     returnType(double())
> > >     r <- dim(cov_mat)[1]
> > >     q <- dim(corr_mat)[2]
> > >     xm_mat <- matrix((x-mu_vec), q, r)
> > >
> > >     logProb <- (-1/2) * (r*q*log(2*pi) + q*logdet(cov_mat) + r*logdet(corr_mat) +
> > >                            sum(diag(inverse(corr_mat) %*% t(xm_mat) %*% inverse(cov_mat) %*% xm_mat)))
> > >     return(logProb)
> > >   }
> > > )
> > >
> > >
> > > ## model with my distribution ---------
> > > rho_codev2 <- nimbleCode({
> > >   # priors on rho1 and rho2
> > >   rho1 ~ dbeta(4,6); rho2 ~ dbeta(4,9)
> > >   constraint_rho ~ dconstraint(rho1 + rho2 < 1)
> > >
> > >   og_mat[1:3,1:3] <- nim_mat(c(1, (rho1 + rho2), rho2, (rho1+rho2), 1, 0, rho2, 0, 1))
> > >   iden[1:3, 1:3] <- diag(3)
> > >
> > >   # likelihood
> > >   for(j in 1:n) {
> > >     y[j,1:9] ~ dMVNkron(mu[1:9], og_mat[1:3,1:3], iden[1:3, 1:3])
> > >   }
> > > })
> > >
> > > rho_v2 <- nimbleModel(rho_codev2, constants = constants, data = data, inits = inits)
> > >
> > > conf_rho <- configureMCMC(rho_v2, useConjugacy = FALSE)
> > > mcmc_rho <- buildMCMC(conf_rho)
> > >
> > > comp_rho <- compileNimble(rho_v2, mcmc_rho, resetFunctions = TRUE)
> > > samples_v2 <- runMCMC(mcmc = comp_rho$mcmc_rho, niter=5000, nburnin = 1000) %>% as.matrix() %>% mcmc()
> > >
> > > plot(samples_v2)
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > >
